**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit right running against us. I checked both planner candidates and swept the full document for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify", "monitor" and "usage":

- **§ 5/6 Compensation (p0047)** — verification runs in our favour only: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges, and we may contest them. No vendor right to examine our records.
- **§ 8 Client covenants** — imposes compliance-with-laws, access-restriction and content warranties, but no inspection or examination right.
- **§ 2(e) (p0037)** — usage statistics and raw log files flow *to* Client, not the reverse.
- **§ 8(f) (p0058)** — the only vendor self-help right ("technical mechanisms" against spamming) operates inside TrueLink's own hosted Interface, so it is neither a usage/records audit nor remote access to Client systems; the walk-away trigger is not engaged.

Because no audit obligation binds us, the rule's parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) cannot be breached — the position sits better than preferred. Inserting an audit clause would manufacture an obligation against our own party, so no edit is warranted. Watch-item for later drafts: if TrueLink adds audit or verification language, hold it to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems (fallback: annual, 15 days' notice, 10% cost-shift threshold).
